title: When the Veil Turns
premise: Freya Underhill has spent her life in the Veiled Valley, where the royal court exiles its food-tasters because magic cannot cross its borders — and where her own strange immunity to poison is quietly feared. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, Freya learns she is the last heir of the covenant that once bound the magical realm of Aethermoor to the mortal world, a covenant broken by the king's own ancestors. Hunted by the king's sorcerers who want the map destroyed, she crosses into Aethermoor, where power tempts her exactly as it corrupted those before her. In the end, Freya reforges the covenant not by claiming the throne-shaped power offered to her, but by shattering it — binding both realms to shared consequence rather than one ruler's will, and choosing to belong to neither world entirely.
about_author: Ines Delacroix is the pen name of a former pastry chef who spent a decade working in castle hotels across Europe before turning to fantasy. She writes about kitchens, courts, and the quiet people history forgets to crown.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the Veiled Valley, Freya survives another poisoned dish meant for an exiled noble, revealing her unnatural immunity and the court's growing suspicion of her. The dying courier staggers into the valley — impossible, since magic cannot follow — and dies pressing a map into her hands as the king's sorcerers breach the border for the first time in a century. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; Freya realizes staying means death, leaving means everything she knows.

chapters.title: Where Magic Remembers Her
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with interludes from sorcerer Captain Aldric hunting her. Crossing into Aethermoor, Freya discovers the land recognizes her blood: doors open, rivers part, and ruins whisper her family name. She finds the half-mad archivist Wren, who explains the broken covenant and the price of reforging it. But using the map's magic feels intoxicatingly easy — her first taste of corruption. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by temptation; belonging offered at a cost she can't yet name.

chapters.title: The Crown-Shaped Hunger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Freya and Aldric, who defects after seeing what the king truly intends: to consume Aethermoor's magic and make himself immortal. Freya reaches the Covenant Spire, where the source of all realm-binding power offers itself to her — enough to save everyone, if she takes the throne-shaped mantle her ancestors corrupted. Aldric arrives not as hunter but as witness. Emotional beat: climax; Freya stands at the exact point where inheritance becomes repetition, and must choose differently than every heir before her.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Consequence
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Instead of taking the power, Freya breaks the Spire's singularity, scattering the covenant into thousands of small bonds — every living thing in both realms now shares the magic's fate, making tyranny self-defeating. The king's claim collapses; Aldric carries the truth home while Freya, no longer fully of either world, becomes the covenant's wandering keeper. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; Freya gains belonging not through a place or a crown, but through responsibility freely chosen.
